                                                                                                                       ┃
   It would also break every regulation he had sworn to follow. A lighthouse that changed its signature was a          ┃
   lighthouse that lied, and mariners trusted the pattern with their lives.                                            ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   But the pattern did not know about the boat.                                                                        ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   He threw the lever. The great lens shuddered and slowed, groaning against the brake. He put his shoulder to the     ┃
   housing and turned it by hand, inch by inch, until the beam lay along the bearing he had memorised in his first     ┃
   year, when old Pettigrew, the keeper before him, had walked him through the channel with a chart and a pipe.        ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   Three degrees west of the red buoy, Pettigrew had said. Remember that, lad. It's the only thing on this rock worth  ┃
   remembering.                                                                                                        ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   Elias held the lens there. His arms shook. The wind howled, and the tower swayed in a way towers were not supposed  ┃
   to sway. He held it for an hour. Then another.                                                                      ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   ────────────────────                                                                                                ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   Dawn came pale and exhausted. The storm had blown itself out, leaving a sea like crumpled iron and a sky washed     ┃
   clean.                                                                                                              ┃
                                                                                                                       ┃
   On the landing, bobbing against the rocks, was a fishing boat. Its mast was snapped and its hull scraped raw. Three ┃
   people sat huddled in the bottom of it, wrapped in oilskins: a bearded man, a woman, and a girl of perhaps nine,    ┃
   her face white with cold.                                                                                           █
                                                                                                                       █
